title: SHCT — Slug–Hydrate Coupled-Transient solver

creators.name: Onyejekwe, Akosa Samuel
creators.affiliation: Cyprus University of Technology, Limassol, Cyprus

description:
A one-dimensional transient solver that carries the slug field and the hydrate field of a subsea multiphase pipeline in a single integration: holdup transport, conservative gas-mass continuity, an implicit pressure equation, energy transport and an advected hydrate phase field, closed by published correlations and a multicomponent Peng–Robinson flash, and advanced over a Monte-Carlo ensemble that returns a probabilistic time-to-plug.

v3.4.0 — hydrate deposits on the WALL area, not the gas–liquid interface. This is the substantive change, and it moves every reported number. The wall growth law used ai, the gas–liquid interfacial area. That is the right term for growth at that interface and the wrong one for a wall process: ai falls toward zero as a line fills with liquid, so the model predicted almost no wall deposit in exactly the liquid-full, oil-dominated configuration where Qin (2020) MEASURES film growth at 0.02–0.08 in/hr. It now uses the wall area, 4/D scaled by the liquid holdup and the water fraction of that liquid. Against that measurement the model moves from 6.5–26× the observed rate to 0.65–2.6×, an implied capture fraction of 0.38–1.54 where the previous form needed an implausible 0.04–0.15. ΦSH is computed from the same area, so the coupling number and the process it describes now refer to the same surface.

The case study moves to late life. With the correction, 35 % water cut at full rate is SUB-critical (ΦSH = 0.27 against Φcrit = 1.08) and does not plug. The study therefore reports 70 % water cut at 0.6× design rate — when hydrate risk actually bites in a mature field — where the line is marginally critical: peak ΦSH 1.95, sustained 1.06 against Φcrit = 1.08, 1.37 km of route super-critical, Pplug = 1.0, P50 time-to-plug 3.72 h (P10 3.02 h, P90 5.96 h), peak deposit 117 mm, max subcooling 24.4 °C, MEG demand at the 60 wt% ceiling over 26.5 km. Not below 0.6×: there the line stops slugging, fslug hits its numerical floor and ΦSH jumps to ~1200, an artefact rather than a result. The engineered fix (restored insulation + continuous MEG) no longer removes the risk — Pplug falls to 0.33, peak deposit 16.4 mm, MEG 45.6 wt%, no-touch time 12.7 h — and is reported that way.

Self-consistency, for the first time. The equilibrium relation δeq = ΦSH · δref (δref = 21.2 mm) predicts 5.94 mm against 3.65 mm actually reached on the sub-critical reference case. Independently, a sweep of water cut and rate puts the bore-closure bifurcation between ΦSH 0.84 and 1.01 — straddling the DERIVED Φcrit = 1.08 on a configuration the threshold was never fitted to.

Verification and evidence. The full suite now passes 5/5 with nothing inconclusive: thermal relaxation 0.0797 % NRMSE (it was 6.188 % and unattributed — the test itself was wrong, leaving the uncertainty sampler on so Uwall was perturbed under it), order of accuracy 0.995, cross-engine agreement, Ransom's water-faucet problem at L1 order 1.04 and 6.1× better than upwind, and a manufactured-solution smooth-order check. Six published trends are reproduced, up from five: the sixth compares film growth rate against the Qin (2020) measurement above, which is what exposed the interfacial-area defect and then supported the kinetics. 104/104 tests pass.

What is still not established. Φcrit is derived and now corroborated by a bifurcation it did not set, but it has not been MEASURED. C, n and kg0 remain unfitted; only the growth magnitude is anchored, through one published film-growth rate. There is no whole-system comparison against a licensed transient multiphase code. On the as-operated case 26.3 % of hydrate formed reaches cells where the wall is at δmax and the bulk at φmax simultaneously and cannot be placed; it is reported in every summary as hydrate_packing_clip_frac and its mechanism is not attributed. The liquid balance closes to 3.6e-15 and the bounds discard is now −1.4e-15, i.e. zero — the 5.85 % discard of earlier releases is gone. Treat this as a hypothesis with a verified solver behind it, not a calibrated predictor.

This release archives the exact code, input deck and generated outputs behind the manuscript A dimensionless coupling number for the competition between hydrate deposition and slug renewal in subsea multiphase pipelines. Earlier releases archive superseded physics; cite this version or the concept DOI.
